These are rates of **areal radius**. The last entry is not an instrument reading of a body passing A at \(16.49c\). Independent integration of \(e/(Fq)\) from \(L(1+\epsilon)\) to D gives \(c|\Delta t|=2608.0964,\ 7243.2714,\ 11848.7386\) for \(\epsilon=10^{-2},10^{-4},10^{-6}\). The integers in §14 are correct.

**3. DERIVED on P7 — what becomes complex and why there are two solutions.** For an interior radius write \(k_r=\sqrt{L/r-1}>0\). The far comparison has
\[
f_r=\pm i k_r,\qquad
\frac1{f_r}=\mp\frac{i}{k_r},\qquad
\frac e{f_r}=\mp i\frac e{k_r}.
\]
A real increment of the supplied \(r\) therefore has a complex inferred radial-ruler component \(dr/f_r\). The corresponding inferred rate and energy components also acquire a phase. Changing the square-root choice conjugates them. Neither \(F\) nor \(q^2\) changes. Choosing the sign of an initial velocity and choosing a root of the frame conversion are independent mathematical operations.

For the incoming body at A, \(f_A=\pm2i\) and the inferred \(\gamma=e/f_A=\mp i/4\). On the \(+2i\) branch, the inferred held-time differential along the body is \((e/f_A)d\tau=-i\,d\tau/4\), while the inferred radial differential is \(dr/f_A=i\sqrt{17}\,c\,d\tau/4\). The other branch conjugates both. Their ratio is \(-\sqrt{17}\,c\) on **both** branches. This is an explicit example of complex clock and ruler components producing a real quotient. It identifies the sense in which this account has motion in a complex dimension. No extra spatial coordinate, proper-time reversal, or second physical body worldline is generated by taking a square root.

**4. DERIVED on P2, P7 and the stated domains — what interior A can measure.** P7 says A’s own reading is real. Local SR in P2 requires a massive body’s co-located \(\gamma_{\rm own}\ge1\). The far-inferred \(\mp i/4\) cannot be that reading. Keeping the subscript is essential. The shortest contradiction if they are identified is
\[
e^2=F_A\gamma_{\rm own}^2,\qquad e^2=1/4,\quad F_A=-4,\quad
\gamma_{\rm own}^2\ge1 .
\]
This uses the manuscript’s local SR import and its own equations. It supplies no objection to the passage just calculated.

One can say more than “A’s reading is unspecified.” Let \(J_A>0\) be A’s **native, locally calibrated radial length per unit of the supplied areal-radius increment** at the encounter. Then \(d\ell_A=J_A\,dr\), and local SR gives
\[
\gamma_{A,\rm own}^2=1+J_A^2(e^2-F_A),\qquad
\frac{v_{A,\rm own}}{c}
=-\frac{J_A\sqrt{e^2-F_A}}{\sqrt{1+J_A^2(e^2-F_A)}}.
\]
For every such calibration, A sees the co-located body moving inward. P7 fixes clock ratios; it supplies no numerical \(J_A\). Substituting \(dr/f_A\) into this *native* length would give an imaginary length for a real \(dr\).

There is also an exact check on attempting to repair this by a single real grid for every body. Put \(h=f_r/f_A\) on A’s side and \(d\ell_r=J(r)dr/h\). If each incoming body is also assigned a real, constant A-normalized count \(e_A=h\gamma_{\rm own}\), local SR and P8 would require
\[
e_A(e)^2=\frac{F}{F_A}+J(r)^2(e^2-F).
\]
Subtract the equations for two distinct incoming counts. Their difference forces \(J^2\) to be constant in \(r\). Differentiate either equation where \(F'\ne0\): it then requires \(J^2=1/F_A=-1/4\). **No real universal radial calibration realizes those identifications.** The decision left to the author is which additional relation would connect a native interior reading to an incoming body’s far count. P8 already decides the areal trajectory, and P7 already decides the two inferred phases.

**5. DERIVED on P8 and local SR — outward check.** The outgoing solution reaches \(L\) with \(+ce\). For \(e<1\) it reaches the outer turning point above; for \(e\ge1\) it escapes. The relative outward boost to marginal escape follows by comparing \(\beta_e=\sqrt{1-F/e^2}\) with \(\beta_1=\sqrt{1-F}\) from the exterior. The limit of \((\beta_1-\beta_e)/(1-\beta_1\beta_e)\) is \((1-e^2)/(1+e^2)\). For the incoming body the corresponding relative escape speed tends to \(c\). For a held frame it also tends to \(c\).

**2. DERIVED on P2, P5, P7 — the far-coordinate light trajectory.** Fix one propagation sign \(\sigma=\pm1\). The two factors for the clock and radial ruler give
\[
\frac{dr}{dt}=\sigma cF,\qquad
c(t-t_0)=\sigma[H(r)-H(r_0)],\qquad

\]
Indeed \(H'=1/F\). For \(\sigma=+1\), the speeds in units of \(c\), at \(1100,1010,1001,1000,999,990,900,200\), respectively, are
\[
0.090909,\quad 0.009901,\quad 0.000999,\quad

The velocity field changes sign exactly at \(L\). It contains \(f^2\), so the two P7 roots give the same numbers. Also \(H\to-\infty\) from both sides. On either open interval \(H\) is strictly monotone. The exterior image is all of \(\mathbb R\), while \(H((0,L))=(-\infty,0)\).

This establishes precisely what the far clock can say about a turn. The two signs of the velocity **across the edge** are established. A photon arriving at \(L\) and reflecting at a finite far time would require a solution of \(\dot r=\sigma c(1-L/r)\) that reaches its equilibrium at finite time. The integral rules this out; equivalently the right-hand side is smooth at \(L>0\), so the solution initialized at \(L\) at finite \(t\) is \(r=L\). P8’s passage has no such far-time description. This conclusion uses no GR causal cones.

**3. DERIVED on P7 — exterior time intervals inferred by A.** For an exterior static branch the held clock at D has \(d\tau_D=f_D\,dt\). Converting a duration of the same static-time interval to the inferred A scale gives
\[
d\widehat T_A=\frac{f_A}{f_D}d\tau_D=f_A\,dt=\pm2i\,dt .
\]
Thus, for the outward exterior segment from \(1000+\delta\) to D,
\[
c\,\Delta\widehat T_A
=\pm2i\left[100-\delta+1000\ln(100/\delta)\right] .
\]
At \(\delta=10,1,0.1,0.01\) the coefficients of \(\pm i\) are \(4785.1702,\ 9408.3404,\ 14015.3106,\ 18620.6607\). This is a computable two-valued inference about an exterior interval. It gives no imaginary tick to the clock physically held at 200.

**4. DERIVED on P2, P5, P7 — the native A account on its own side.** The real held-clock ratio there is \(h(r)=f_r/f_A=\sqrt{F/F_A}\). In static synchronization, let \(X_A\) be radial length on A’s calculation grid. Then
\[
d\tau_r=h\,dT_A,\qquad d\ell_r=\frac{dX_A}{h},\qquad
\frac{dX_A}{dT_A}=\sigma c\,\frac{F}{F_A}.
\]
The outgoing local speed at A is \(c\); its native grid speed at B is \(c/36\). B measures \(c\) on its own instruments. With \(J(r)=dX_A/dr\), the A-time for its outward photon is
\[
\boxed{c[T_A(r)-T_A(200)]=\int_{200}^{r}J(u)\,\frac{F_A}{F(u)}\,du,\qquad 200\le r<L .}
\]
The manuscript gives the circumferences and clock ratios. A circumference difference does not measure the radial distance between the spheres on A’s native grid. There is a straightforward exterior check on this distinction. For a static exterior reference P, \(dT_P=f_Pdt\) and \(dX_P=dr/f_P\), so \(c\,dT_P/dr=f_P/F\) for an outgoing ray. Merely using \(F/F_P\) as the speed in the original \(r\) gives \(F_P/F\) for the reciprocal and misses one power of \(f_P\). At the interior A, the formal \(dr/f_A\) is a complex inference. It cannot calibrate \(J\) as a real native length.

**Calculated calibration example, outside the manuscript derivation.** To exhibit how much the missing measurement matters, take a constant native grid calibration \(J=\kappa>0\), use the static synchronization above and set \(T_A(200)=0\). This is an optical calculation on A’s side:
\[
cT_A(r)=-4\kappa[H(r)-H(200)] .
\]
At B this gives \(5517.7662\,\kappa\). At \(990,999,999.9,999.99\) it gives \(14368.1065\,\kappa,\ 23542.4469\,\kappa,\ 32749.1873\,\kappa,\ 41959.1677\,\kappa\). For each finite \(T_A\ge0\) there is exactly one state on this emitted inner leg, approaching C as \(T_A\to+\infty\). The conclusion about this interval holds also for a positive continuous \(J\) with a finite nonzero limit at C. Its coefficient and its finite times depend on the calibration.

There is a physical reason to keep this example out of the manuscript as a universal clock-and-ruler repair. If one also reuses the same real areal spheres and the original flux prescription with \(h^2=F/F_A\), the inferred native outward holding law is \(r^2 h g_{\rm hold}=G\mathcal M/(F_A J)\), negative for positive \(J\). The all-body test in A.4 independently gives \(J^2<0\). Thus choosing \(\kappa=1\) by convention does not produce a jointly consistent matter, flux and photon theory inside.

**5. DERIVED — joining the two sides and the state at C.** Even on the far grid, integrating the clock gives two constants,
\[
ct_{\rm in}=\sigma H+C_{\rm in},\qquad
ct_{\rm out}=\sigma H+C_{\rm out}.
\]
Rate ratios cannot determine \(C_{\rm out}-C_{\rm in}\). Equal offsets in radius give \(H(L+\delta)-H(L-\delta)=2\delta\). Unequal offsets \(a,b>0\) give
\[
H(L+b)-H(L-a)=a+b+L\ln(b/a).
\]
As the offsets shrink this finite part depends on their ratio. Neither limit is an elapsed crossing time; each one-sided travel integral to C diverges. Even on one side a change of remote synchronization \(T_A\mapsto T_A+\chi(r)\), \(\chi(200)=0\), preserves A’s actual clock and all fixed-station rate ratios.

**Answer about every A-time and the edge.** On the calibrated emitted inner leg just calculated, every finite time after emission has a state, and C occurs at no finite time. In v0.75, A’s own clock ticks are real, the exterior interval assigned through P7 has the two values calculated above, and no rest clock exists at C. The premises supply **no unique real all-times map** \(T_A\mapsto\) photon state covering both legs, no prescribed match of their offsets, and no native A timestamp at the edge. The author’s hint that the far-time sign flip should generate such a map encounters a specific mathematical step: an equality of squared rates determines neither a native radial calibration nor an additive clock synchronization. The decision about adding such a rule belongs to the author. Section 14, Parts 5–8

# The check: one route through the event horizon

## What the author asked, word for word

After your audit of draft v0.75 (exchange audit75; your Part II is copied below), we reported to the author and asked him three questions. He answered, 26 November 2026, word for word:

"1.  the turn as the far observer sees it (derived now),
2. yes
3. yes"

Answer 1 chose, for the paper, your result on the body falling in: the turn as the far observer sees it (the far time runs backward inside \(L\), and the inside part of the path runs back toward \(L\) on that clock). Answer 2 says yes to this question of ours: "Shall Codex check the route around L (±iπL/c) as the rule that joins the two sides?"

## The route, as we stated it to the author (ours, not yet checked)

"Premise 8's integral for the far time of the passage cannot be taken straight through L (it has a pole there). Taken around the pole in the complex plane, it gains ±iπL/c (numerically ±3,141.6 for L = 1,000, for matter and for light). The two ways around the pole are the two solutions. The real part runs backward inside. It also says how the two sides of L join, which Codex found the premises leave open."

Our numerical check: the integral of \(c\,dt/dr=-e/(Fq)\) (body, \(e=0.5\)) and of \(c\,dt/dr=1/F\) (light) along half circles of radius 1 and 0.01 about \(r=L=1{,}000\), above and below, gives an imaginary part \(\pm3{,}141.5927\) on the two half circles and a real part of \(6\) and \(0.06\) (body) or \(-2\) and \(-0.02\) (light), going to zero with the radius.

## What to check

### 1. The continuation and its real part

**DERIVED on the two passage integrals.** Write \(z=r-L\). Fix the orientation **from exterior to interior**, from \(z=b>0\) to \(z=-a<0\). Let \(s=+1\) denote the upper detour and \(s=-1\) the lower. For matter take the branch with \(q(L)=e>0\).

Both integrands have a simple pole. Their regular parts can be isolated exactly:
\[
\begin{aligned}
-\frac{e}{Fq}
&=-\frac1F-\frac1{q(e+q)}
=-\frac{L}{z}-1-\frac1{q(e+q)},\\[2mm]
\frac{\sigma}{F}
&=\frac{\sigma L}{z}+\sigma .
\end{aligned}
\]
The first identity follows from \((e-q)(e+q)=F\). Thus, writing \(c\,dt/dr=R/z+h(z)\), the residues are \(R=-L\) for the inward body and \(R=\sigma L\) for light. In each case \(h\) is analytic near the detour and real on the real radius. The matter detour stays clear of any zero of \(q\).

A continuous logarithm changes by \(\ln(a/b)+s i\pi\). The regular part has a primitive through zero. Consequently the **exact endpoint difference** is
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
c\Delta t
=R\bigl[\ln(a/b)+s i\pi\bigr]+\int_b^{-a}h(z)\,dz .}
\]
The last integral can be taken on the real interval because its integrand is regular there.

- **Fixed endpoints.** Deforming the detour without changing its winding or crossing another singularity leaves the entire answer unchanged.
- **Equal offsets \(a=b=\rho\).** The imaginary contribution is exactly \(s i\pi R\) for every admissible \(\rho\). The real contribution depends on \(\rho\) and tends to zero. For light it is exactly \(-2\sigma\rho\). For the body \(h(0)=-1-1/(2e^2)\), so at \(e=0.5\) the leading real term is \(6\rho\).
- **Unequal offsets.** As \(a,b\to0\) with \(a/b\to k>0\), the real difference tends to \(R\ln k\). For light the exact real difference is \(\sigma[L\ln(a/b)-a-b]\). Thus the rule matches the *regular parts* at C. It preserves the logarithmic difference between unequal endpoints.

Direct integration on the semicircles gives the following values. The final column is the coefficient of \(i\).

| Exterior-to-interior arc, \(L=1000\) | \(\rho\) | \(\operatorname{Re}(c\Delta t)\) | \(\operatorname{Im}(c\Delta t)\) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Inward body, \(e=0.5\) | 1 | \(6.00000933337\) | \(-s\,3141.592654\) |
| Inward body, \(e=0.5\) | 0.01 | \(0.0600000000093\) | \(-s\,3141.592654\) |
| Light, \(\sigma=+1\) | 1 | \(-2\) | \(+s\,3141.592654\) |
| Light, \(\sigma=+1\) | 0.01 | \(-0.02\) | \(+s\,3141.592654\) |

The reported \(6\) and \(0.06\) are rounded matter values. The reported light values are exact. Traversing the same arc in reverse negates the entire increment.

### 2. Why the matching is an added rule

**DERIVED on P7 and P8.** Choose a real regular primitive \(U\) with \(U'=h\) and \(U(0)=0\). On each open real interval the time equation integrates to
\[
ct=R\ln\left|\frac{r-L}{L}\right|+U(r-L)+C_{\rm side}.
\]
Changing \(C_{\rm in}\) leaves every P7 clock ratio, every P8 differential equation and the infinite far-clock time at C unchanged. That freedom is the exact step the existing premises leave open.

**DERIVED on the ADDED RULE.** Continuing the exterior primitive fixes
\[
\boxed{C_{\rm in}-C_{\rm out}=s i\pi R.}
\]
Its real part is zero in the common normalization above. Each one-sided time integral to C still diverges. The finite complex endpoint difference assigns a relation between the branches while preserving P8’s result that the far clock records no finite crossing time.

### 3. How the two contours correspond to P7’s two roots

**DERIVED on P7 and the common-contour rule.** Near C, \(F=z/(L+z)\). The denominator has an analytic logarithm there and is positive at the real endpoints. Starting with \(f>0\) outside therefore gives, inside,
\[
\log F=\ln|F|+s i\pi,\qquad
f=\exp\!\left(\tfrac12\log F\right)=s i\sqrt{|F|}.
\]

| Exterior-to-interior route | Interior \(f\) | Imaginary term in \(ct\), inward body | Imaginary term in \(ct\), light |
|---|---|---|---|
| Upper | \(+i\sqrt{|F|}\) | \(-i\pi L\) | \(+\sigma i\pi L\) |
| Lower | \(-i\sqrt{|F|}\) | \(+i\pi L\) | \(-\sigma i\pi L\) |

**On the two prescribed detours there is a one-to-one correspondence.** For the inward body the upper route gives a positive imaginary clock root and a *negative* imaginary time offset. For light with \(\sigma=+1\) both imaginary signs are positive on the upper route. Changing the direction of propagation changes the residue’s sign. Choosing the other clock root leaves the direction of propagation unchanged.

P7 alone cannot recover the contour choice with its winding information. For a path with argument change \((2n+1)\pi\), the interior root is \(i(-1)^n\sqrt{|F|}\), whereas the time offset is \(i(2n+1)\pi R/c\). Arguments \(\pi\) and \(5\pi\), for example, produce the same clock root and different times. This is why “no additional winding” matters in the rule.

For \(\sigma=+1\), \(\operatorname{Re}t\to-\infty\) at C from both sides. The real velocity \(dr/d\operatorname{Re}t=cF\) changes sign there. For \(\sigma=-1\), both signs reverse.

## A. A held frame’s own ruler inside \(L\)

### 1. What the clock, flux and mass laws fix

**DERIVED — P5 and P7 on A’s side.** Write
\[
F=1-\frac Lr,\qquad k(r)=\sqrt{-F(r)},\qquad
k_A=2,\qquad F_A=-4,\qquad
h(r)=\frac{f_r}{f_A}=\frac{k(r)}{k_A}>0.
\]
Both half-turns give the same \(h\). In particular \(h(A)=1\) and \(h(B)=1/6\). In the static synchronization of audit75 B.4, the local held clock and ruler satisfy
\[
d\tau_r=h\,dT_A,\qquad
d\ell_{\rm own}=\frac{dX_A}{h}=\frac{J(r)}{h(r)}\,dr.
\]
Thus \(J=dX_A/dr\) is the calibration of **A’s grid**, and the requested **local** calibration is \(J_{\rm own}=J/h\). Setting \(h(A)=1\) establishes \(d\ell_{\rm own}=dX_A\) at A. Identifying either of those lengths with \(dr\) takes another step.

**DERIVED — P1, P3 and §4, statements 2 and 6.** The flux test supplies more information than the clock ratios alone. Take \(d\ell_{\rm own}\) positive outward. The signed acceleration needed to hold a frame at \(r\) is
\[
g_{\rm hold}
 =c^2\frac{d\ln h}{d\ell_{\rm own}}
 =\frac{c^2}{J(r)}\frac{dh}{dr}.
\]
Since \(h^2=F/F_A\),
\[
2h\frac{dh}{dr}=\frac{L}{F_A r^2}.
\]
The sphere has area \(4\pi r^2\) on the unchanged transverse rulers. Its counted holding pull in **A’s units** is therefore
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
4\pi r^2 h g_{\rm hold}
 =\frac{4\pi G\mathcal M_\infty}{F_A J(r)},\qquad
\mathcal M_\infty=\frac{c^2 L}{2G}.}
\]
P1 requires the same enclosed count on every one of these spheres outside the source. Thus **\(J(r)=\kappa\) is constant**. The entire family of positive real rulers allowed by the same-side flux, clock and relative mass laws is
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
dX_A=\kappa\,dr,\qquad
d\ell_{\rm own}=\frac{\kappa}{h(r)}\,dr
=\frac{2\kappa}{\sqrt{L/r-1}}\,dr,\qquad \kappa>0.}
\]

**DERIVED — the absolute mass test, P5 and P7.** If A’s mass is obtained by converting the real far count through P7, the result assigned to A is
\[
\widehat{\mathcal M}_A=\frac{\mathcal M_\infty}{f_A}
=\mp\frac{i}{2}\mathcal M_\infty .
\]
Requiring the signed flux just calculated to equal \(4\pi G\widehat{\mathcal M}_A\) fixes
\[
\frac{1}{F_A\kappa}=\frac{1}{f_A}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\kappa=\frac{1}{f_A},\qquad d\ell=\frac{dr}{f_r}.
\]
This is exactly **R2**. The flux and mass equations even recover its phase. P7 assigns that phase to the inference across the boundary. A’s own weighing and ruler reading are real.

There is a short way to see why the distinction is necessary. Identifying a real nonzero \(\mathcal M_A\) with that conversion would require \(\mathcal M_\infty^2=F_A\mathcal M_A^2=-4\mathcal M_A^2\). No real choice of ruler can satisfy this equation. Taking A as the Gaussian observer is legitimate and fixes the same-side variation \(\mathcal M_{\rm held}(r)=\mathcal M_A/h(r)\). At A, where \(h=1\), that equation returns \(\mathcal M_A\) itself. It supplies no independent value for A’s native source count.

## What remains open and what could decide it

- **A’s native normalization.** The missing step is one real calibration of \(dX_A/dr\), obtainable in the thought experiment from the A–B–A round trip. Relating a native weighing of the enclosed source to the exterior count also requires a rule distinguishing the signed flux, its magnitude and the cross-boundary inferred mass. R3 supplies a candidate length calibration. P7 already supplies the complex inference.
- **The material ruler.** On §17’s specified grid the consequences are derived. An independent test of that grid identification would measure the circumference difference of adjacent held shells, their local radial separation and their clock rate \(f\), and check \(\Delta C/(2\pi\Delta\ell)\to f\). For the comparison with GR’s interior equations, a confirmed surface line from the specified class with \(\sqrt3-1<z<2\) would refute the manuscript’s combined bound while lying within the GR comparison range. No raw observation deciding that test was supplied here.
- **The shared one-way horizon in GR.** The exterior clock, ruler and pole equations do not require GR’s same-mass continuation or its single one-way boundary. P8 gives passage in both directions in finite body time, and the adopted contour gives the two far inferences. The discriminating observation remains exterior reception of light or matter whose origin inside \(r=L\) for the independently identified enclosed count is established. The native A–B timing experiment and the contour arithmetic answer different, fully specified parts of that comparison.

### 1. One closed charged-particle cycle, counted twice

**Setup X.** A fixed Gaussian surface encloses the source, both stations, the charges and their field, the lifting and braking equipment, and the work store. Write \(H\) for the local reference energy of any housing that travels with the pair. This keeps the author’s \(m\) equal to the mass of the particles. The complete transported energy in the load’s own frame is
\[

The electrostatic configuration and its field are two ways of calculating the same \(U\).

**Manuscript count — DERIVED, C and P1–P5.** At a held station the transported entry is \(fQ\). The local holding force on the compact load is \(Qg_{\rm hold}/c^2\). Converting the incremental work into far units at the place where it is done gives
\[
dW_A=f\,\frac{Q}{c^2}g_{\rm hold}\,d\ell
     =fQ\,d\ln f=Q\,df .
\]
Thus \(W_{\rm up}=Q(f_2-f_1)\). The conversion \(U\to K\) at the top changes the two far entries by \(-f_2U\) and \(+f_2K\), which sum to zero.

On the descent the load’s centre of mass starts at rest at station 2. P3 gives \(\gamma_{\rm bulk,1}f_1=f_2\) just before braking at station 1. The **bulk** kinetic energy delivered to the brake, in \(A\)’s units, is therefore

This is separate from the **internal** \(K\) that restores the charge configuration at the bottom. The bottom reset changes the internal entries by \(-f_1K+f_1U=0\). The internal work store has delivered and recovered the same independently calculated work. §4, clock, work and free-body count

a_{\rm hold}=c^2\frac{d\ln N}{d\ell},\qquad
dW_A=N\,\frac{Q}{c^2}a_{\rm hold}\,d\ell=Q\,dN.

This is §8, part 10’s independent local-force check, now applied to the complete load. One can check which energy enters it directly. A7 includes the electromagnetic field in \(T\). The integral gives \(NQ\) in the compact-load limit, including the store on ascent and the internal motion on descent. ### 3. Shell assembled at fixed \(R\)

**Manuscript — DERIVED, C and §4 statement 5.** With \(m\) the accumulated local rest mass, put \(a=G/(Rc^2)\). The shell’s far-counted mass \(M\) satisfies
\[
\frac{dM}{dm}=\sqrt{1-2aM},\qquad M(0)=0 .
\]
Differentiating the square root gives \(d\sqrt{1-2aM}/dm=-a\). Consequently
\[

\]
Against the separated-at-infinity reference, the lowering equipment receives
\[

=\frac{Gm_0^2}{2R}.
\]
Thus \(Mc^2+W_A=m_0c^2\). The negative binding contribution is already in \(M\). At \(am_0=1\), \(R=L\) and \(M=m_0/2\), the limiting result stated in the manuscript. §4, shell derivation and recipient of the work

**GR — comparison IMPORT, with its material assumption stated.** Section 7 solves the vacuum on either side of a shell. To calculate a *material* shell’s mass from its proper energy, one needs a matching equation. Take a neutral thin round shell, empty regular interior, ordinary exterior branch, and include all surface energy in \(m_0c^2\). At a moment of time symmetry use proper radial distance \(\ell\). The GR spherical constraint is
\[
{}^{(3)}R=\frac{2[1-(r')^2-2rr'']}{r^2}
=\frac{16\pi G}{c^2}\rho,\qquad
\rho=\frac{m_0}{4\pi R^2}\delta(\ell-\ell_R),

where the prime denotes \(d/d\ell\). Integration gives \(r'_- - r'_+=Gm_0/(Rc^2)\). The empty regular interior gives \(r'_-=1\), and the outer vacuum gives \(r'_+=\sqrt{1-2GM/(Rc^2)}\). Thus GR gives exactly the same mass and binding contribution on this branch. Neglecting the binding in the GR count would contradict its own material-shell equation. This comparison uses no GR ruler inside the manuscript derivation. Israel, thin-shell matching

The infinite-separation reference is an energy comparison, not material that can be imported through a finite sealed surface during the experiment. F_{\parallel}=1-\frac{2\lambda D}{D^2-a^2},\qquad

## Part II. The repairs and derivations

### 1. What the general bridge charges

Let \(E_{\mathrm h}\) be an energy read by a held frame, and let \(f\) convert it to \(A_\infty\)’s energy units. For a free massive body, §4 gives
\[
E_{\mathrm h}=\gamma m_0c^2,\qquad
E_\infty=fE_{\mathrm h},\qquad
e=f\gamma.
\]
Between two held stations in the domain of this real conversion,
\[
I_g=\int_1^2\frac{\mathbf g\cdot d\boldsymbol\ell}{c^2}
=\ln\frac{\gamma_2}{\gamma_1}
=\ln\frac{f_1}{f_2}.
\]
Here \(d\boldsymbol\ell\) is measured on the encountered station’s ruler and \(\mathbf g\) denotes the pull in the work integral. In the field-free acceleration calculation, let the force, displacement and \(m=\gamma m_0\) all be evaluated in the specified field-free inertial account. Then
\[
I_F=\int_1^2\frac{\mathbf F\cdot d\boldsymbol\ell}{mc^2}
=\int_1^2\frac{d(mc^2)}{mc^2}
=\ln\frac{\gamma_2}{\gamma_1}.
\]
This proves the bridge for matched energy ratios. Both integrals are **dimensionless**. In the field-free account the energy actually supplied is \(m_0c^2(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)\). The displacement in that work calculation is measured in the frame in which the force generates the motion. Switching the observer of an already moving body supplies no such displacement or work history.

The exact scale accounting, valid also for a nonconstant local store, is
\[
\boxed{dE_\infty=f\,dE_{\mathrm h}+E_{\mathrm h}\,df},
\qquad
\Delta E_\infty
=f_2(E_{\mathrm h,2}-E_{\mathrm h,1})
 +E_{\mathrm h,1}(f_2-f_1).
\]
For the free body the terms cancel at every step. In §2’s kinetic and potential entries the cancellation reads
\[
\Delta\!\left[f(\gamma-1)m_0c^2\right]
 +m_0c^2\Delta f
=m_0c^2\Delta(f\gamma)=0 .
\]
Both terms are in \(A_\infty\)’s units. This verifies the balance for that trade without counting the potential release twice. The same calculation on one interior side uses a fixed interior reference station \(a\), \(h=k/k_a\), and gives \(\Delta(h\gamma)=0\) in that station’s units.

If a ledger **does** substitute a fixed \(f_*\) for the changing scale of a free body, the unbalanced change it records is
\[
\Delta E_{\mathrm{frozen}}
=f_*m_0c^2(\gamma_2-\gamma_1).
\]
It is positive when \(\gamma_2>\gamma_1\). Conversely, assigning a scale change to a locally fixed entry \(E_{\mathrm h}\) changes the reference ledger by \(E_{\mathrm h}\Delta f\). Calling this a physical surplus requires the specified ledger to acquire that entry without the corresponding transfer. Section 1 supplies exactly this test for the store \(U\). With \(\Delta f=f_2-f_1>0\), the far-account work returned less work supplied is
\[
(mc^2+K)\Delta f-(mc^2+U)\Delta f
=(K-U)\Delta f=0.
\]
Omitting \(U\) on ascent gives the stated spurious \(+U\Delta f\). This is an actual computation of the omitted term and its sign.

**The exact failed inference in §9.3** is the move from “no frame held at rest” to “nothing in it charges a body or an energy” if the latter is asserted of all transfers. In the frozen-scale calculation, \(f_*\), \(\gamma_1\) and \(\gamma_2\) are defined readings. In GR’s interior held-frame test, the proposed observer fails normalization. Consequently the corresponding \(E_{\mathrm h}\,df\) is undefined. Setting that term equal to zero, retaining a nonzero gain, and attributing the difference to GR would introduce a new accounting law. The general bridge takes the derivation as far as this exact result: **the continuation removes the observer needed to implement the compensating scale update, so it fails the manuscript’s held-frame count inside \(L\).**

### 2. The release, the clock and the match at \(L\)

For \(0<r_0<L\), an interior held frame reads the released body at
\[
\gamma(r)=\frac{k_0}{k(r)},\qquad k_0^2=\frac L{r_0}-1.
\]
Since \(k\) increases inward, an inward step would give \(\gamma<1\). On the allowed side, let \(v_{\mathrm h}=d\ell/dt_{\mathrm h}\) be the local radial speed as the body passes a held frame. Local special relativity gives \(dt_{\mathrm h}/d\tau=\gamma\) and hence
\[
\frac1{c^2}\left(\frac{d\ell}{d\tau}\right)^2
=\frac{\gamma^2v_{\mathrm h}^2}{c^2}=\gamma^2-1 .
\]
Using the real held ruler \(dr=k\,d\ell\) gives
\[
\boxed{\dot r^2=c^2 k^2(\gamma^2-1)
=c^2(k_0^2-k^2)
=c^2L\,\frac{r-r_0}{r r_0}},\qquad \dot r=\frac{dr}{d\tau}.
\]
Section 14.10 supplies the outward pull at release. In local ruler units its magnitude is
\[
-c^2\frac{d\ln(k/k_0)}{d\ell}\bigg|_{r_0}
=\frac{c^2L}{2r_0^2 k_0}>0.
\]
On the departing solution, differentiating the radial equation gives \(\ddot r=c^2L/(2r^2)\). Its release value is exactly \(k_0\) times the local acceleration, as \(dr=k\,d\ell\) requires at rest. This supplies the direction and start of motion using the manuscript’s own pull.

The outward proper-time integral has the explicit value
\[
\begin{aligned}
c[\tau(r)-\tau(r_0)]
&=\sqrt{\frac{r_0}{L}}\int_{r_0}^{r}\sqrt{\frac{x}{x-r_0}}\,dx\\
&=\sqrt{\frac{r_0}{L}}\left[
\sqrt{r(r-r_0)}
+r_0\,\operatorname{arcosh}\sqrt{\frac r{r_0}}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Differentiation recovers the integrand, and the expression vanishes at release. The initial inverse-square-root singularity is integrable. At \(L\), \(k=0\), and the outward limit is \(\dot r=ck_0\).

The junction uses the meaning of **at \(L\)** in premise 8. The interior solution has a left derivative \(ck_0\) there. Premise 8 assigns the body’s speed at that same circle, on that same clock, the value \(c e_{\mathrm{out}}\) on departure. A derivative at the crossing must agree with its one-sided derivative. For the positive exterior count,
\[
\boxed{e_{\mathrm{out}}=k_0.}
\]
This identifies the precise condition that makes the proof work. Two curves can meet continuously at \(L\) with unequal slopes. The manuscript supplies the stronger statement of a body-clock speed at the crossing. No held observer at \(L\) is used.

There is also a direct construction verifying the match. Set \(q=k_0\). The real outgoing motion in the two accounts can be written compactly as
\[
\dot r^2=c^2(q^2-|F|).
\]
Inside, this is the equation derived with the real ruler. Outside, it is premise 8 with \(e_{\mathrm{out}}=q\). The exterior solution is given near \(L\) by
\[
\tau(r)-\tau(L)=\int_L^r\frac{dx}{c\sqrt{q^2-F(x)}}.
\]
It exists for every \(q>0\) in an exterior neighborhood of \(L\). Its initial derivative is \(cq\), giving a differentiable crossing when joined to the calculated interior solution. One further consequence is that the one-sided radial accelerations at \(L\) are \(+c^2/(2L)\) inside and \(-c^2/(2L)\) outside. The speed matches exactly.

**The account distinction in the preceding §14.6 paragraph is essential.** The far observer infers an interior count \(e_{\mathrm{inf}}=\pm i k_0\). Substitution into the far-inferred equation gives
\[
c^2(e_{\mathrm{inf}}^2-F)
=-c^2(k_0^2-k^2)
=-\dot r_{\mathrm{real,in}}^{\,2}.
\]
At the crossing its limiting square is \(-c^2k_0^2\). The real body-clock calculation gives \(+c^2k_0^2\). Thus the result actually established is \(e_{\mathrm{out}}=|e_{\mathrm{inf}}|\). Identifying the two interior squared rates as the same real measurement would produce a sign error. Using a single real \(e=k_0\) in the far-inferred formula throughout the interior would already give \(2c^2k_0^2\) at release, where the body is at rest. The passage’s real-ruler derivation avoids both errors.

Outside, the turning and escape results follow from
\[
\dot r^2=c^2(e^2-1+L/r).
\]
For \(0<e<1\) the outer turning radius is \(L/(1-e^2)\); the exterior acceleration \(-c^2L/(2r^2)\) points inward there. For \(e\ge1\) there is no finite outer turning radius. At infinity \(f\to1\), so \(\gamma_\infty=e\) and the speed in the far frame is \(c\sqrt{1-e^{-2}}\).

Finally, on the outgoing exterior branch,
\[
\frac{dt_\infty}{dr}
=\frac{e}{cF\sqrt{e^2-F}}
=\frac{L}{c(r-L)}+O(1/c).
\]
Thus \(t_\infty=(L/c)\ln[(r-L)/L]+O(1)\) as \(r\downarrow L\). This verifies the sign of the far-time divergence and the distinction from the finite proper time.

### 3. The fixed mass, the missing held frame and the conserved momentum

**GR comparison only.** In §7’s solution \(\xi=\partial_t=\partial_v\) has norm \(-Fc^2\). A held observer would require \(u=\alpha\xi\) and hence
\[
-c^2=g(u,u)=-\alpha^2Fc^2 .

Outside, \(\alpha=1/\sqrt F\). At \(L\) the direction is null. Inside it is spacelike, and no real \(\alpha\) satisfies the normalization. This proves the incompatibility for the specified observer independently of the choice between the displayed coordinate systems.

Outside, the held observer’s proper acceleration has magnitude
\[
a_{\mathrm{held}}=\frac{c^2 F'}{2\sqrt F}
=\frac{GM}{r^2 f}.
\]
The weighing operation specified in §4.2 therefore gives \(a_{\mathrm{held}}r^2/G=M/f\), while the metric still contains the parameter \(M\). This verifies §9.2’s distinction. It also checks where the alternative \(1-L/(2r)\) in that statement comes from. The manuscript’s exterior clock and ruler give \(df/dr=g_{\mathrm{held}}/c^2\). Inserting \(GM/r^2\) as the *held* pull and imposing \(f(\infty)=1\) gives \(1-L/(2r)\). Inserting \(GM/(r^2f)\) instead gives \(f^2=1-L/r\). For the radial test body in §9.3, write the GR symmetry charge as \(e_{\rm GR}=-u\cdot\xi/c^2\). Inside, \(s=\xi/(ck)\) is a unit spatial direction. The corresponding local momentum component is
\[
p_{\hat s}=m_0u\cdot s=-\frac{m_0c\,e_{\rm GR}}{k}.

This makes “becomes a momentum” precise. The conserved quantity is proportional to the momentum conjugate to the spacelike symmetry coordinate. The local orthonormal component itself varies with \(k\). The radial moving observer of §9.3 with zero symmetry charge measures
\[

\]
At fixed nonzero \(e_{\rm GR}\) that reading varies with radius even though \(M\) is fixed. It supplies an explicit check against identifying the one mass parameter with frozen readings for all observers. It does not implement the missing held observer’s accounting procedure.

On the manuscript’s definition, **the same-mass continuation and the requirement of an interior held-frame count are mathematically incompatible**. Neither evaluates a pair of complete before-and-after held-frame counts in §2’s units. Accordingly there is no interior numerical \(\mathcal R_E\) from this comparison. The zero residual for the fully accounted §1 machine and the positive error \(U\Delta f\) for its deliberately omitted store are both calculable.

For momentum, the manuscript’s complete isolated system on the common time \(T\) has, under premise 6,

=\Delta\sum_i\mathbf p_i
=\int_{T_1}^{T_2}\sum_i\mathbf F_i(T)\,dT=0 .

This is the balance imposed by P. The release calculation tracks one body and supplies no separate evolution of source recoil. GR’s conserved symmetry momentum is a different quantity from this complete-system vector.

This is Part 6’s real reading, including for a body that entered from outside.

**DERIVED \([C,S,R]\).** The held ruler and local clock give

\[
\gamma^2-1=\frac{1}{c^2}\left(\frac{d\ell}{d\tau}\right)^2
=\frac{\dot r^{\,2}}{c^2a^2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\dot r^{\,2}}{c^2}=
\begin{cases}
e^2-F,&r>L,\\
q^2-k^2,&0<r<L .
\end{cases}
\]
At \(L\) the one-sided speed magnitudes are \(ce\) and \(cq\). **DERIVED \([X]\).** Both counts are positive, so speed matching gives \(q=e\). This proves the boxed law. It also explains exactly what “the same count” means here. The real exterior count and the real interior count match. Multiplying the *real interior* \(\gamma\) by the *complex* \(f\) instead gives \(\pm i e\).

**Exact error in Law I.** Substituting \(F=-k^2\) directly in the exterior equation gives \(\dot r_{\rm I}^{\,2}=c^2(e^2+k^2)\). Substituting that result back into the real ruler and the real SR identity gives
\[
(\gamma k)^2=k^2+\dot r_{\rm I}^{\,2}/c^2=e^2+2k^2 .
\]
This changes with \(r\), in direct conflict with Part 6’s \(\gamma k=q\). Law I inside is the signed continuation of the exterior equation and is exactly the GR interior radial geodesic equation on the comparison side. The manuscript’s real interior readings derive Law II.

The ruler’s role can also be checked without fixing its scale in advance. If \(d\ell=\lambda\,dr/k\), \(\lambda>0\), the same calculation gives \(\dot r^2=c^2(q^2-k^2)/\lambda^2\). Matching at \(L\) gives \(q=\lambda e\), and the inner turn is \(L/(1+\lambda^2e^2)\). Thus the turn already follows for every positive scale. The adopted value \(\lambda=1\) fixes its radius for a specified exterior \(e\).

## Part II. Consequences

### The turns, the return and the body’s time

**DERIVED \([F,C,S,R,X,A]\).** The exact first integral and its acceleration on each moving segment are
\[
\frac{\dot r^{\,2}}2+\frac{c^2}{2}(|F|-1)
       =\frac{c^2}{2}(e^2-1),\qquad
\ddot r=-\operatorname{sgn}(F)\frac{c^2L}{2r^2}.
\]
The effective potential in this rewriting is \(-G\mathcal M_{\rm enc}/r\) outside and \(+G\mathcal M_{\rm enc}/r-c^2\) inside. The velocity is continuous at passage. The one-sided accelerations at \(L\) are opposite.

The allowed radii satisfy \(|F|\le e^2\). Hence
\[
r_-=\frac{L}{1+e^2},\qquad
r_+=\frac{L}{1-e^2}\quad(0<e<1).
\]
At \(r_-\), \(k=e\) and the real held frame reads \(\gamma=1\). The inward motion has reached rest. In particular,
\[
\dot r^{\,2}=c^2L\frac{r-r_-}{rr_-},\qquad
r-r_-=\frac{c^2L}{4r_-^2}(\tau-\tau_-)^2
       +o\big((\tau-\tau_-)^2\big).
\]
Part 10 supplies the strictly outward pull on release there. This matters mathematically because a squared first-order equation in isolation also permits waiting at a zero. The free-release dynamics selects immediate reversal. The body crosses \(L\) outward with the same \(e\). For \(0<e<1\) it subsequently turns at \(r_+\) and repeats the radial motion. For \(e\ge1\) it reaches arbitrarily large radius. **Every finite \(e>0\) has \(r_->0\). No body obeying this own-clock law reaches the centre.**

For any monotone leg,
\[
c\Delta\tau=\left|\int_{r_1}^{r_2}\frac{dr}{\sqrt{e^2-|F|}}\right|.
\]
Here are explicit primitives for the general solution. Inside, with \(b=1+e^2\),
\[
S_i(r)=
\frac{\sqrt{r(r-r_-)}+
r_-\operatorname{arsinh}\sqrt{(r-r_-)/r_-}}{\sqrt b}.
\]
Thus \(c\Delta\tau_{L\to r_-\to L}=2S_i(L)\). Outside, a primitive \(S_o\) is
\[
S_o(r)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{r_+}{\sqrt{1-e^2}}\bigl(\theta-\sin\theta\cos\theta\bigr),
\quad \theta=\arcsin\sqrt{r/r_+},&0<e<1,\\[4pt]
\dfrac{2r^{3/2}}{3\sqrt L},&e=1,\\[5pt]
\dfrac{\sqrt{r(r+d)}-d\,\operatorname{arsinh}\sqrt{r/d}}{\sqrt{e^2-1}},
\quad d=L/(e^2-1),&e>1 .
\end{cases}
\]
Differentiation gives \(S_i'=1/\sqrt{e^2-k^2}\) and \(S_o'=1/\sqrt{e^2-F}\). Both tend to \(1/e\) at \(L\). At each finite turn the inverse-square-root singularity is integrable. For a bound body the full own-clock period is \(2[S_i(L)+S_o(r_+)-S_o(L)]/c\).

### Far time and the two solutions

**DERIVED \([T,F]\) with the radial law.** Put \(w=\sqrt{e^2-|F|}\) and \(\sigma=\operatorname{sgn}\dot r\) on a moving leg. Then
\[
\dot r=\sigma cw,\qquad
\frac{dt}{d\tau}=\frac eF,\qquad
\frac{dr}{dt}=\sigma c\frac{F}{e}w.
\]
Far time runs forward outside and backward inside along increasing \(\tau\). On infall \(dr/dt\) changes from negative outside to positive inside. On return it is negative inside and positive outside. There are **two distinct effects**. The far-time orientation flips at \(L\), where \(|\dot r|=ce\). The body reverses on its own clock at \(r_-\), where \(\dot r=0\).

**DERIVED \([T,J]\), with finite parts matched at \(L\).** The far-time differential has the exact decomposition
\[
c\frac{dt}{dr}=\sigma J_e(r),\qquad
J_e(r)=\frac{e}{Fw}
=\frac{L}{r-L}+1+\frac{\operatorname{sgn}F}{w(e+w)}.
\]
The coefficient of the pole is independent of \(e\). For the real part define
\[
P(r)=L\ln\left|\frac{r-L}{L}\right|
+\int_L^r\left[1+
 \frac{\operatorname{sgn}F(u)}{w(u)[e+w(u)]}\right]du .
\]
This matches the finite constants at equal \(|r-L|\), continues the logarithm on the prescribed half-turn, and uses each side’s own differential for the regular part. Write \(\eta=+1\) for the upper exterior-to-interior half-turn and \(\eta=-1\) for the lower. With \(t(D)=0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
ct_{\rm in}(r)&=P(D)-P(r) &&(r>L),\\
ct_{\rm in}(r)&=P(D)-P(r)-\eta i\pi L &&(r<L),\\
ct_{\rm out}(r)&=P(D)+P(r)-2P(r_-)-\eta i\pi L &&(r_- \le r<L).
\end{aligned}
\]
The incoming real part tends to \(+\infty\) at \(L\) from either side. The returning real part tends to \(-\infty\) there from either side. **Neither passage has a finite far-clock time.** At the ordinary turn \(r_-\), the continued time is finite and continuous, with the same imaginary part on arrival and departure.

There is a precise limit to analytic continuation here. After subtracting \(L/(r-L)\), the exterior and interior limits of \(J_e\) are
\[
1+\frac{1}{2e^2},\qquad 1-\frac{1}{2e^2},
\]
respectively. One meromorphic differential with that simple pole cannot have these two different regular coefficients. The half-turn of the common logarithm gives exactly the manuscript’s offset. If the joining rule means analytic continuation of the whole exterior differential, it conflicts with Law II. The finite-part match above is the consistent implementation used for the figures.

For a **single complex time carried through both crossings**, there is a further sign to track. Returning on the inverse half-turn restores the positive exterior clock root. The radial sign has also reversed, so the return crossing adds another \(-\eta i\pi L/c\). The exterior return then has the listed real part and an accumulated offset \(-2\eta i\pi L/c\). An outward leg normalized independently to real exterior time has its own time origin. Neither convention assigns a finite elapsed far-clock time through \(L\).

**DERIVED \([C,S,R,T,J]\).** Inside, \(f=\eta i k\). The far observer’s inferred held-clock and ruler steps are
\[
\gamma_{\rm inf}=\frac e f=-\eta i\,\frac e k,\qquad
d\theta_{\rm inf}=\frac e f\,d\tau,\qquad
d\ell_{\rm inf}=\frac{dr}{f}=-\eta i\,\frac{dr}{k}.
\]
Each differs from the corresponding real local reading by the same phase \(-\eta i\). Their ratio is consequently real,
\[
\frac{d\ell_{\rm inf}}{d\theta_{\rm inf}}
=\frac{\dot r}{e}=\sigma c\,\frac{w}{e}.
\]
These equations locate the complex dimension exactly. The two inferred steps and the continued far time are complex conjugates across the two choices. The areal derivative \(\dot r\) on the body’s clock is real.

### Conservation and the GR comparison

**DERIVED \([C,S,R,X]\), manuscript accounting.** On either side, in the real normalization of that side, the two terms counted once give
\[
a(\gamma-1)m_0c^2+a\,m_0c^2=e\,m_0c^2 .
\]
In the units of a particular held interior observer at \(R\), divide both sides by \(k(R)\). The motion realizes this balance: substituting \(\dot r^2/c^2=e^2-a^2\) into the real SR identity gives \(a\gamma=e\) throughout each leg, including at the turn by continuity. The body returns to D with the same mass-energy entry and opposite radial momentum. The calculation verifies the body’s energy entry. Section 3 premise 6 supplies the closed-system momentum law; the fixed-source trajectory specifies no recoil history with which to calculate a separate total-momentum residual.

**IMPORT, GR comparison only.** Match the source, \(L\), initial D event, inward velocity and exterior \(e\). The same-mass Schwarzschild continuation uses \(e=F\dot t\) and timelike geodesic normalization,
\[
-c^2=-Fc^2\dot t^{\,2}+\frac{\dot r^{\,2}}F
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\dot r_{\rm GR}^{\,2}=c^2(e^2-F).
\]
Inside, wherever the manuscript’s body can go,
\[
\dot r_{\rm GR}^{\,2}-\dot r_{\rm II}^{\,2}=2c^2k^2.
\]
At the manuscript’s turn, GR predicts \(\dot r_{\rm GR}^{\,2}=2c^2e^2\). For this body that is \(0.5c^2\), with inward velocity in the future black-hole interior. The manuscript predicts **zero velocity followed by outward motion**. Thus the exterior radial equation, the same incoming state and the same speed at \(L\) do **not** require GR’s interior continuation. The two interior predictions already differ at an explicitly calculated event.

For the manuscript’s Section 2 count, the continued GR metric requires a held observer \(u=\alpha\partial_t\) to satisfy \(\alpha^2F=1\). For \(F<0\) there is no real such observer. The continued solution therefore cannot realize the interior held-observer count of §9 statement 3. On GR’s own comparison side the Killing quantity there is a momentum component. The established conservation discrepancy is the absence of the required observer and count; the calculation yields no numerical amount of energy lost. The manuscript identifies the deciding observation as “anything, light or matter, arriving outside from inside an event horizon.” No such observation is supplied in this run.

## Part V. What remains open

1. **Meaning of continuation for the regular part of matter’s far time.** Matching its one-sided finite parts gives the explicit result above. If full analytic continuation is required, the unequal regular coefficients demonstrate an obstruction. If only the logarithmic offset is prescribed and the finite parts are left unmatched, one additive real constant between sides remains unspecified.
2. **A single globally real far-clock label for the complete return.** Positive exterior \(f\), continuity of the chosen root and one continuous complex \(t\) give the accumulated return offset calculated in Part II. Assigning real exterior time on both legs additionally requires an identification of the two exterior clock origins. This affects absolute far-time labels. It does not enter the return radius, proper time, count, rates or either horizon limit.

**Verdict.** The manuscript’s Part 6, its adopted ruler and premise 8 select **Law II everywhere inside \(L\)**. The \(e=0.5\) body crosses inward, turns at **800**, and crosses outward after **\(1488.6543/c\)** of its own time between crossings, carrying **\(e=0.5\)**. The far observer’s time flips at \(L\); the two inferred clock and ruler solutions are complex conjugates. GR’s same-mass interior continuation predicts continued inward motion at the very radius where the manuscript’s body comes to rest and reverses.

5.6 The speed a frame needs to escape

An independent Claude check of the reply of 5.5 and of draft v0.84, made by an agent that had not seen our own check, derived the law of free motion inside \(L\) for itself, agreed with the auditor’s derivation and reproduced every number in the reply and in the draft by two methods. It disagreed with one claim of the reply: that the speeds a moving frame still needs at \(L\) to escape keep their derivation from outside \(L\). Under the one law every body that goes inward comes back out with its count, so a frame falling in needs, along its motion, only what a frame on its way out needs. Its derivation steps went to the auditor word for word, for a targeted check and repair with the same prompt; the message held the prompt (Part 2), the author’s rules 7 to 9 (Part 2) and the manuscript’s passages that the check needs, word for word, and the parts of its run block that are not copies of those texts are given here word for word, followed by the reply. Run: 647,308 input tokens (617,984 of them cached), 15,199 output tokens, 6.6 minutes. The auditor agreed: under the one law the least push at \(L\) is the same for a frame falling in and a frame on its way out with the same count, \(c(1-e^2)/(1+e^2)\) along its motion for \(e\lt1\) (\(0.6\,c\) inward for \(e=0.5\), after which the frame turns at \(L/2\) and goes away for good) and none for \(e\ge1\); the value \(c\) is the limit for turning a frame that is falling in back at \(L\) itself, which no finite push reaches; and a frame in free motion needs less than \(c\) at every radius it reaches. It agreed with every step of the check but one inference: premise 4 alone does not make the count inside \(L\) equal to the count outside; premise 3 at the real size of the clock rate does, which the paper now names. It made one precision: that a body cannot go deeper than its turn rests on no ruler, while its arrival there and its reversal also use the law of motion and the outward pull. Sections 3, 14 and 18 carry the correction.

2. **The match at \(L\).** Which premise makes the real count inside \(L\) equal to the count outside (the speed \(c\,e\) on both sides): premise 8, premise 4, premise 3 at the real size of the clock rate, or the ruler rule? Label the step.
3. **The turn without a ruler.** Is the existence of the inner turn derived from the readings of the frames held at rest alone (premises 3 and 7, with \(\gamma\ge1\)), with a ruler needed only for its radius? Derive it.
4. **The far clock.** State exactly the step that gives \(dt/d\tau=e/F\) inside \(L\) (real, negative), and the alternative the check names.
5. **For every step:** the label (DERIVED, with the premise or statement it uses; ADDED RULE; IMPORT; HINT), every number checked, and the frame of every figure. General relativity's equations are on the comparison side only, labelled as such; its interior decides nothing about the manuscript's side (Section 0, item 1). The passage through \(L\), in both directions, is premise 8: never refuse it.

## D. The independent check's derivation steps, word for word

**A.6 The match at L.**
- From outside, |ṙ| → ce. From inside, |ṙ| → cq.
- The free body passes L (premise 8), and nothing acts on it there (premise 4: it keeps its clock and ruler). So the rate at which it passes the circles on its own clock does not jump, and q = e.
- The same follows from premise 3 at the real size of the clock rate: |γf| = e outside and γk = q inside. This is the step the ruler rule takes for the ruler.
- **DERIVED** [premise 8, premise 4, or premise 3 at real size]. Premise 8's words say that the body passes, not with what speed. What makes the two speeds equal is premise 4 or premise 3.

**A.8 Turns.**
- The body turns where |F| = e²: r₋ = L/(1 + e²) inside, where the held frame reads γ = 1, and r₊ = L/(1 − e²) outside for e < 1.
- At r₋ the outward pull (Part 10: its direction from premises 3 and 7, for every real ruler) makes the rest a reversal. The squared law alone would also allow the body to stay at r₋.
- The turn exists without any ruler. γ = q/k ≥ 1 (H2) gives k ≤ q, so r ≥ L/(1 + q²) > 0. A ruler is needed only to fix q in terms of e: a scale λ gives q = λe and a turn at L/(1 + λ²e²), and the ruler rule gives λ = 1.
- Nothing with e > 0 reaches the centre.
- **DERIVED.**

**A.11 Escape speeds.**
- Every body that goes inward comes back out with its count (A.7, A.8). So escape for good means count ≥ 1, in either direction.
- Frame held at rest at r, with a = √|F|: it needs c√(1 − a²).
  - Outside that is c√(L/r) = √(2GM/r).
  - Inside, for L/2 ≤ r < L, it is c√(2 − L/r).
  - From L/2 or deeper it needs nothing.
  - On both sides the needed speed rises to c only at L.
- Free frame with count e < 1 at radius r: a boost along its motion raises its count to e′ = a cosh(|η| + β).
  - The speed needed for e′ = 1 is c·tanh(arccosh(1/a) − arccosh(e/a)).
  - At L this tends to c(1 − e²)/(1 + e²), **whether the frame is falling in or on its way out**.
  - At its turns it is c√(1 − e²). It is below c at every radius the frame reaches.
  - For e ≥ 1 it needs nothing.
  - Reversing a frame that is falling in at L needs c. That is the value v0.84 states, and it is not the least speed for escape under the one law.
- **DERIVED** [A.7, A.2].

**A.12 The far clock.**
- Take the far observer's own time t and the radius r as real.
- The far observer works out the held clocks and rulers as dT = f dt and dℓ = dr/f (premise 5 with premise 7's f). The count is kept in its units, γ_inf·f = e (premise 3).
- So dt/dτ = e/F on both sides of L: positive outside, a pole at L, negative inside. Time flips.
- This is the convention Part 10 uses for light, dr/dt = cf² = cF.
- If one instead converts the held frames' own real clock step, dt = γ_loc dτ/f, the increments are imaginary: dt/dτ = ±ie/F. The paper does not use that route.
- **DERIVED** on the Part 10 convention.

## Part I. The speeds needed to escape

**Under the adopted one law, the least boost at \(L\) is the same size for a freely falling frame and a freely outgoing frame of the same count \(e\).** For \(0<e<1\), its magnitude is \(c(1-e^2)/(1+e^2)\), directed **along the frame’s motion**. For \(e\ge1\), the required boost is zero. At \(e=0.5\), the falling frame needs **\(0.6c\) inward**. That boost raises its count to one. It then turns at \(L/2\), crosses \(L\) outward and escapes for good. The \(c\) in draft v0.84 is the limiting requirement for **immediate outward reversal** of an ingoing frame at \(L\).

The manuscript specifies the setup in §14 Part 5. “Its numbers below are on its own clock and in the radius of the circles, with \(e\) in the far observer's units.” I use that radius \(r\), body time \(\tau\), fixed \(L=2G\mathcal M_{\rm enc}/c^2\), one boost measured locally at one event, and free motion thereafter. Escape for good means that the subsequent trajectory goes to arbitrarily large \(r\). The calculation proceeds from the radial law to the escape criterion, from local boost composition to the minimum, and from the held-frame readings to a separate audit of the match and turn. The checks are substitution at the threshold, the two limits at \(L\), and the quoted numerical trajectories.

### 1. Which post-boost counts escape?

**DERIVED \([C,J,A]\).** Write \(e'\) for the count immediately after the boost. In the exterior,
\[
\frac{\dot r^{\,2}}{c^2}=e'^2-1+\frac Lr .
\]
For \(e'<1\) there is a finite outer turning radius \(L/(1-e'^2)\). For \(e'=1\), the outgoing branch has \(\dot r=c\sqrt{L/r}>0\) at every finite exterior radius and goes to infinity. For \(e'>1\), it also goes to infinity. An initially inward branch turns at \(L/(1+e'^2)\) and returns with the same count, as verified in Part II. Hence
\[
\boxed{\text{Escape for good}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ e'\ge1}
\tag{1}
\]
for the radial free motions in question, in either initial direction. The equality in (1) matters for a *least* speed.

### 2. Frame held at rest

**DERIVED \([C,H,J,A]\).** At \(a>0\), launch speed \(u\) in the held frame gives \(e'=a/\sqrt{1-u^2/c^2}\). If \(a\ge1\), release at rest already meets (1). Otherwise solving \(e'=1\) gives
\[
\boxed{
\frac{u_{\rm held}}c=
\begin{cases}
\sqrt{L/r},& r>L,\\
\sqrt{2-L/r},& L/2<r<L,\\
0,&0<r\le L/2 .
\end{cases}}
\tag{2}
\]
Outside this is \(\sqrt{2G\mathcal M_{\rm enc}/r}\) in speed units. Both one-sided limits at \(L\) are \(c\). This is a held-frame **limit**. The held clock factor itself vanishes there. Equation (2) reproduces the manuscript’s rest-frame result throughout its stated domains.

### 3. Frame in free motion, inward or outward

**DERIVED \([C,H,J,A]\).** First take \(a>0\) and \(a\le e<1\). The magnitude of the frame’s rapidity relative to the held frame is \(\eta=\operatorname{arcosh}(e/a)\). A boost of rapidity magnitude \(b\), measured in the free frame and directed along its motion, gives
\[
e'_{\max}=a\cosh(\eta+b)
         = e\cosh b+\sqrt{e^2-a^2}\sinh b .
\tag{3}
\]
This is a maximum at fixed boost size. In local boost composition, a boost at angle \(\theta\) to the initial motion multiplies the second term by \(\cos\theta\le1\). The aligned radial launch attains the bound and has the escaping trajectory of (1). At a turn the second term vanishes, and either radial direction gives the same threshold.

Setting (3) equal to one therefore gives the minimum
\[
\boxed{
u_{\rm free}(r,e)=
\begin{cases}
c\tanh\!\left[\operatorname{arcosh}(1/a)-
                    \operatorname{arcosh}(e/a)\right],&0<a\le e<1,\\
0,&e\ge1,\quad a\le e .
\end{cases}}
\tag{4}
\]
The domain \(a\le e\) is precisely the set of radii the frame can reach. At either turn for \(e<1\), (4) gives \(c\sqrt{1-e^2}\).

The limit at \(L\) can be taken **before** solving for the boost. Let \(s=\operatorname{sgn}\dot r\), let \(b_{\rm out}\) be signed rapidity with outward positive, and put \(p=\dot r/c\). Local boost composition gives the finite expressions
\[
e'=e\cosh b_{\rm out}+p\sinh b_{\rm out},\qquad
p'=p\cosh b_{\rm out}+e\sinh b_{\rm out}.
\]
At the crossing \(p\to se\). Thus \(e'\to e\exp(s b_{\rm out})\) and \(p'\to s e'\). For \(0<e<1\), the threshold is \(b_{\rm out}=s\ln(1/e)\), giving
\[
\boxed{\frac{u_{\rm signed}(L,e)}c
       =s\,\frac{1-e^2}{1+e^2}.}
\tag{5}
\]
No finite boost reverses the sign of \(p\) at that crossing. If an ingoing frame is required to launch **immediately outward** onto an escaping trajectory, the required exterior boost magnitude is \(c\tanh[\operatorname{arcosh}(e/a)+\operatorname{arcosh}(1/a)]\). That tends to \(c\). It answers a different minimization from (1).

## Part II. The match at \(L\), the turn without a ruler and the far clock

### 1. What fixes the match

**DERIVED \([C,H,R,J]\).** Before matching, write the interior held reading as \(\gamma_{\rm loc}=q/k\). Part 6’s ratio of two *interior* readings fixes the constancy of \(q\). To see separately what the ruler supplies, use the manuscript’s comparison scale \(d\ell=\lambda\,dr/k\), \(\lambda>0\) constant. H2 gives
\[
\frac{\lambda^2\dot r^{\,2}}{c^2}=q^2-k^2,\qquad
|\dot r|_{L^-}=\frac{cq}{\lambda},\qquad
|\dot r|_{L^+}=ce .
\tag{6}
\]

There are two ways to read the match in the supplied mathematics.

- **Count route — DERIVED from premise 3 at the real size, with premise 7’s phase conversion.** In the far calculation \(\gamma_{\rm inf}=e/f\). With \(f=\pm ik\) and \(\gamma_{\rm loc}=|\gamma_{\rm inf}|\) as specified in §3 and §14 Part 7, \(k\gamma_{\rm loc}=k|e/f|=e\). Thus \(q=e\). With the real ruler \(\lambda=1\), (6) gives \(ce\) on both sides.
- **Speed route — DERIVED from the adopted common crossing speed and the ruler.** Equation (6) gives \(q=\lambda e\) if the two crossing speeds match. The manuscript’s ruler then gives \(q=e\). This is the route used where Part 6 identifies \(e=k_0\) on emergence.

**Passage alone does not fix the derivative.** Premise 8’s statement that the body passes and premise 4’s statement that its own clock and ruler are kept do not, by themselves, equate the two one-sided derivatives of the circle radius. For example, the separate first integrals with \(\lambda=1,\ e=1/2,\ q=1\) admit a continuous ingoing join with limiting derivatives \(-c/2\) and \(-c\) on the same parameter \(\tau\). The adopted one law excludes that corner. To exclude it *from the bare passage argument*, continuity of \(dr/d\tau\), or an equation excluding an impulse in that quantity, would be an **ADDED RULE**. The count route above needs no such addition.

Thus **premise 3 applied across \(L\) at the real size fixes the common real count**. The ruler converts that count into an areal speed. The full adopted premise-8 equation already incorporates the match. Premise 4 supplies no independent matching equation.

### 2. Exactly how much of the turn follows without a ruler

**DERIVED \([C,H]\).** The held readings give
\[
1\le\gamma_{\rm loc}=\frac qk
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
k^2\le q^2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
r\ge R=\frac{L}{1+q^2}>0 .
\tag{7}
\]
At \(R\) the held frame reads \(\gamma=1\). Thus **the forbidden inner region, centre exclusion for every finite positive count, and the rest radius for a known interior \(q\) follow without a ruler**. If the match is made by the real-count route, \(R=L/(1+e^2)\) follows without a ruler as well.

**DERIVED \([H,R,A]\).** Finite-time arrival and subsequent reversal add a dynamical step. For every constant ruler scale of (6),
\[
q^2-k^2=\frac{L(r-R)}{rR},\qquad
d\tau=\frac{\lambda}{c}\sqrt{\frac{rR}{L}}\,
                   \frac{|dr|}{\sqrt{r-R}} .
\tag{8}
\]
The integral converges at \(R\). Differentiating (6) on a moving branch gives \(\ddot r=c^2L/(2\lambda^2r^2)>0\). Part 10’s outward pull at rest selects immediate reversal there. The squared equation alone also admits waiting at \(R\). In particular, \(\gamma\ge1\) alone is an inequality on positions and contains no travel time or departure rule.

If the exterior speed is held fixed at \(ce\) while the interior ruler scale is varied, (6) gives
\[
q=\lambda e,\qquad R=\frac{L}{1+\lambda^2e^2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Equation (9) is the manuscript’s **scale branch**. Keeping the entire adopted one law at all interior radii requires \(q^2-k^2=\lambda^2(e^2-k^2)\) for varying \(k\), which fixes \(\lambda=1,\ q=e\). The existence of the reversal is independent of the choice among the regular constant scales. The readings-only proof establishes (7); equations (8) and the pull at rest complete the reversal proof.

### 3. Which clock gives real negative \(dt/d\tau\)

**DERIVED \([C,T]\).** Use the *same far-inferred held-clock step* in the two conversions:
\[
\frac{dT_{\rm inf}}{d\tau}=\frac e f,\qquad
dT_{\rm inf}=f\,dt
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{\frac{dt}{d\tau}=\frac{e}{f^2}=\frac eF.}
\tag{10}
\]
Both roots give the same rate. It is positive outside, negative inside and has a pole at \(L\). The alternative in D inserts the held frame’s **own real step**, \(dT_{\rm loc}/d\tau=e/k\), into \(dt=dT_{\rm loc}/f\). It gives
\[
\frac{dt}{d\tau}=\frac{e}{kf}
                  =\frac fk\,\frac eF
                  =\pm i\,\frac eF\qquad(r<L).
\tag{11}
\]
The difference is the numerator clock reading. At B for \(e=0.5\), (10) gives \(-4.5\), and (11) gives \(\mp4.5i\) for \(f=\pm i/3\).

With \(s=\operatorname{sgn}\dot r\) and \(w=\sqrt{e^2-|F|}\), (10) gives
\[
\frac{dr}{dt}=s\,cF\,\frac we,\qquad
\frac{dt}{dr}=\frac{s e}{cFw}
             =\frac{sL}{c(r-L)}+O(1/c)\quad(r\to L).
\tag{12}
\]
The far time tends to \(+\infty\) on the inward passage and \(-\infty\) on the outward passage. The body takes finite proper time through \(L\) since \(w\to e>0\). Inside, **the far-time increments are real** on (10). Part 10’s logarithmic joining convention can also assign \(t\) a constant imaginary offset on a leg. Calling the entire joined value of \(t\) real would omit that offset.

### Matched GR and conservation comparison

**IMPORT \([G_{\rm R}]\), comparison only.** The premise tested is the continuation of one Schwarzschild metric with the same mass through \(L\) for the matched future-ingoing orbit. Fix the count from the same exterior initial data, \(e_{\rm GR}=e\). In GR, radial proper-time normalization and the static symmetry charge give
\[
-c^2=-Fc^2\dot t^{\,2}+\dot r^{\,2}/F,\qquad
F\dot t=e,\qquad
\dot r_{\rm GR}^{\,2}=c^2(e^2-F).
\]
At the manuscript’s inner turn \(F=-e^2\). Consequently,
\[
\boxed{\dot r_{\rm manuscript}=0,\qquad
       \dot r_{\rm GR}=-\sqrt2\,ce}
\]
on the matched ingoing orbit. At \(e=0.5,\ r=800\), these are \(0\) and \(-0.707107c\), each in circle radius per unit body proper time. The GR branch has no inner zero. For the boosted example \(e'=1\), the manuscript trajectory returns from 500; the matched GR branch is still ingoing there. This is the discrepancy produced by continuing \(F\) in the radial law where the manuscript obtains \(|F|\).

**On the manuscript’s count**, \(k\gamma_{\rm loc}=e\) is constant on each free interior leg and the same \(e\) returns. The intentional boost changes the body’s count from \(e\) to \(e'\). If one tests the GR interior trajectory **with the manuscript’s held ruler and H2**, its inferred held count would obey
\[

## Part V. What remains open

There is **no missing calculation for the requested escape speeds on the adopted one law**. Two narrower claims have an identifiable missing implication if asserted independently of that law.

1. A derivation of the common crossing speed **from premise 4 and passage alone** would need an equation enforcing continuity of \(dr/d\tau\) at \(L\). The manuscript’s real-count match and adopted ruler already give the speed by a separate route.
2. A derivation of **finite-time reversal from held energy readings alone** would need an evolution relation connecting those readings to progress in circle radius and selecting departure at rest. Equations (7)–(8) locate the distinction exactly, and the manuscript’s ruler and outward pull complete the derivation.

The mathematical correction to v0.84 is the falling-frame entry in §3 and its two repetitions in §18. For eventual escape at \(L\), both moving frames need \(c(1-e^2)/(1+e^2)\) for \(0<e<1\), and zero for \(e\ge1\). The held-frame limit remains \(c\).
